notes: 32 tissue samples from 5 donors (390C, 403C, 412C, 423C, 428C) across multiple tissues (Blood, BM, Liver, Lung, Spleen, mLN, tLN, Ileum). Parent population for Step 1 is pre-gated T cells (CD3+; enforced by the upstream 'T cells' gate in the source FCS workspace). Th1 sub-gating uses CD127 vs CD69 — in tissue contexts CD69 reports tissue residency (Trm) rather than purely early activation, so this sub-gate probes the Trm-like state of Th1 in the tissue microenvironment. This is the key biological difference from the sister FR-FCM-Z74D_hc cohort, which uses CD127 × PD-1 at Step 9.

steps.note: CD4/CD8 quadrant split on pre-gated T cells (CD3+ enforced upstream by the 'T cells' FCS gate). CD4: CD4+ CD8- (helper T cells). CD8: CD4- CD8+ (cytotoxic T cells). CD4p_CD8p: CD4+ CD8+ (DPT; rare, often thymic emigrants or activated transitional). CD4n_CD8n: CD4- CD8- (DNT; includes γδT, MAIT, iNKT). Useful co-markers: αβ/γδ TCR markers are not in this panel, so DNT cannot be further resolved here.

Classical Sallusto/Lanzavecchia CD8 memory scheme (CCR7 × CD45RA). Naive_CD8: CCR7+ CD45RA+ (antigen-inexperienced). CM_CD8: CCR7+ CD45RA- (central memory; lymph-node homing retained). EM_CD8: CCR7- CD45RA- (effector memory). EMRA_CD8: CCR7- CD45RA+ (terminally differentiated effector memory re-expressing CD45RA). Tissue context: in non-lymphoid tissues (Liver, Lung, Ileum) the Naive_CD8 fraction is expected to be low — a substantial Naive_CD8 signal in those tissues may indicate blood contamination; lymphoid tissues (Spleen, mLN, tLN, BM) are expected to retain more Naive_CD8. Useful co-markers: CD45RO / CD27 / CD28 would refine memory staging but are not in panel; CD69 + CD103 (both in panel) identify tissue-resident memory (Trm) and are resolved separately at Step 9 for the Th1 compartment.

Treg vs conventional CD4 split. tot_Treg: Foxp3+ CD127lo (classical Treg signature — master-regulator TF Foxp3 combined with IL-7Rα down-regulation). non_Treg: Foxp3- (any CD127) — conventional CD4. Useful co-markers: CD25 (IL-2Rα) is a widely used surface Treg marker (Foxp3+ CD127lo CD25+ is a commonly used operational definition) and IS available in this panel — useful as a supplementary QC axis. Helios further stratifies Treg lineage stability downstream (Step 10; see Step 10 note for the contested-marker caveat).

CD4 non-Treg memory subsets (Sallusto/Lanzavecchia, CCR7 × CD45RA). Naive_CD4: CCR7+ CD45RA+. CM_CD4: CCR7+ CD45RA- (central memory; lymph-node homing retained). EM_CD4: CCR7- CD45RA- (effector memory). EMRA_CD4: CCR7- CD45RA+ (terminally differentiated; rare in CD4). Tissue context: the CM_CD4 fraction tends to be enriched in lymphoid tissues (Spleen, LN) due to CCR7-driven homing; non-lymphoid tissues tend to be dominated by EM_CD4 and EMRA_CD4.

T follicular helper identification on memory CD4. CXCR5 is the B-cell follicle homing receptor and the canonical Tfh marker. PD-1 further stratifies Tfh activation state (germinal-center Tfh are PD-1 high). Tfh: CXCR5+ PD-1 intermediate (circulating / resting Tfh). Tfh_hi_PD1: CXCR5+ PD-1 high (activated / germinal-center-like Tfh). non_Tfh: CXCR5- (non-follicular memory CD4). Scope: parent is memory CD4 non-Treg (CM+EM+EMRA); Naive_CD4 and Treg are excluded. Tissue context: Tfh_hi_PD1 is expected to be most enriched in secondary lymphoid tissues (tLN, mLN, Spleen) where germinal centers form. Useful co-markers: ICOS and BCL6 are additional widely used Tfh markers but are not in this panel.

Chemokine-receptor-based Th polarization on non-Tfh memory CD4. Th1: CXCR3+ (any CCR6) — IFNγ producers; T-bet driven; by this definition Th1 also absorbs the plastic Th1/17 ('Th1*') subset (CXCR3+CCR6+, IFNγ+IL-17+). Th17_22: CXCR3- CCR6+ — IL-17 / IL-22 producers without Th1 co-polarization; includes both classical Th17 and Th22, resolved at Step 7 by CCR4/CCR10. non_17_22_1: CXCR3- CCR6- (Th2 candidates and uncommitted effectors; Th2 resolved at Step 8 by CCR4). Design caveat (important): the CXCR3+ definition of Th1 absorbs CXCR3+CCR6+ events (the Th1/17 'Th1*' plastic subset). This inflates Th1 frequency relative to a strict CXCR3+CCR6- Th1 definition, and propagates to the downstream Th1 residency-state analysis (Step 9, CD127 × CD69), which is therefore performed on a Th1 compartment that contains Th1/17 plasticity events. If Th1/17 needs to be isolated, consider a 4-way CXCR3×CCR6 split here — no new reagents required. Useful co-markers: canonical transcription factors (T-bet for Th1, RORγt for Th17, GATA3 for Th2) are not in panel, so classification relies on chemokine receptors alone. This definition matches the sister FR-FCM-Z74D_hc plan (v2) for cross-cohort comparability.

Splitting the CCR6+ compartment (now restricted to CXCR3- CCR6+ by the updated Step 6 definition, so Th1/17 plasticity events do not reach this step). Th17: CCR4+ CCR10- (classical IL-17-producing Th17; skin/mucosa homing via CCR4). Th22: CCR10+ (any CCR4) — IL-22-producing Th22; skin-homing via CCR10, typically CCR4+ as well. Tissue context: Th17 is expected to be enriched in barrier tissues (Ileum, Lung); Th22 is most classically described in skin but is also reported in gut. Useful co-markers: CXCR3- CCR6+ already enforced by parent gate; functional IL-17 / IL-22 intracellular cytokine staining would provide direct functional confirmation but is not in this panel.

Th2 identification within the CXCR3- CCR6- compartment. Th2: CCR4+ (CCR4 is the GATA3-driven Th2-associated chemokine receptor). Only the CCR4+ (Th2) population is explicitly labeled — CCR4- events in this parent remain unannotated by this step because the CCR4- remainder is not a defined cell type. Axis design caveat: the y_marker is CD8, but parent is CD4+ CD8- (all cells are CD8-low by construction at Step 1), so CD8 serves as a purity sanity-check axis rather than a discriminator — the Th2 call is driven entirely by CCR4 on x. Useful co-markers: CD294 (CRTH2) is a widely used surface Th2 marker but not in panel; functional Th2 confirmation would require CRTH2 / GATA3 / intracellular IL-4, none of which are in-panel. CCR4+ is also expressed on Th17, but CCR6+ cells were already removed upstream by the non_17_22_1 parent gate, so CCR4+ at this step specifically marks Th2.

Th1 residency / memory-maintenance state (CD127 × CD69 quadrants) — the key tissue-specific sub-gate of this cohort. Parent note: under the updated Step 6 definition, 'Th1' includes CXCR3+CCR6+ (Th1/17 plastic) events — CD127 × CD69 distributions here reflect a mixture of classical Th1 (CXCR3+CCR6-) and Th1/17; if a pure Th1 residency profile is needed, a 4-way Step 6 split should be used upstream. CD127 (IL-7Rα) is a homeostatic / memory-maintenance receptor retained on stable memory T cells. CD69 in non-lymphoid tissues is widely used as a tissue-resident memory (Trm) marker (rather than purely early activation as in blood); together with CD103 it forms one of the most commonly used Trm signatures, though CD69 alone is not sufficient to define residency, and CD103-negative Trm populations have been described in several tissues (e.g. liver, airway). Th1_CD127p_CD69p: CD127+ CD69+ (tissue-resident Th1 with homeostatic signaling retained — Trm-like Th1). Th1_CD127p_CD69n: CD127+ CD69- (non-resident / circulating memory Th1). Th1_CD127n_CD69p: CD127- CD69+ (tissue-resident with CD127 down — activated / terminally-differentiated Trm-like). Th1_CD127n_CD69n: CD127- CD69- (non-resident, non-memory-maintenance — transitional/effector). Useful co-markers: CD103 is a widely used second Trm marker and IS in panel — combining CD69+CD103+ further supports a core Trm phenotype in many tissues (noting CD103-negative Trm populations also exist). Tissue interpretation: CD69 means different things in blood vs. tissue — in the Blood samples of this cohort (412C_Blood, 423_Pre-blood), CD69+ should be read as early activation, not residency.

Treg lineage stratification by Helios (Ikaros family TF IKZF2). Treg_Heliosp: Helios+ (enriched for thymus-derived / stable-lineage Treg — note that Helios as a strict thymic-origin marker is contested; Helios expression can also be induced in peripherally-generated Treg under certain activation conditions [e.g. Gottschalk et al. 2012, Akimova et al.], so 'Helios+' is best read as 'enriched for stable-lineage Treg' rather than a definitive tTreg marker). Treg_Heliosn: Helios- (peripherally-induced Treg or less-stable Treg; may include recently-converted Tconv). The Foxp3 y-axis is a parent-gate visual QC only — parent is already Foxp3+, so all events should sit at Foxp3-high; the actual call is driven by Helios on the x-axis. Tissue context: under the thymic-origin interpretation, Helios- Treg would be expected to be enriched in mucosal tissues (Ileum) where microbiota-driven peripheral Treg induction occurs; this prediction depends on the contested Helios interpretation and should be confirmed from the data rather than assumed.

Treg memory / activation status (binary split). Naive_Treg: CCR7+ CD45RA+ (resting naive Treg; corresponds to Miyara Fraction I — CD45RA+Foxp3-low resting Treg). Memory_Treg: all other quadrants aggregated — effector/activated Treg (mixture of Miyara Fractions II [CD45RA-Foxp3-high effector Treg] and III [CD45RA-Foxp3-low non-suppressive / cytokine-producing Treg]). This step collapses CM/EM/EMRA into a single 'memory' bucket, unlike the 4-way split used for conventional CD4/CD8 (Steps 2 & 4). Tissue context: Naive_Treg is expected to dominate in lymphoid tissues (Spleen, LN); non-lymphoid tissues are expected to be memory-biased.

Treg tissue-residency / homing quadrants. CCR4 marks skin/mucosa-homing capacity and is enriched on tissue-homing Treg. CD69 in non-lymphoid tissues is associated with a Trm-like residency phenotype. Treg_CCR4p_CD69p: CCR4+ CD69+ (skin/mucosa-homing, tissue-resident-like Treg). Treg_CCR4p_CD69n: CCR4+ CD69- (skin/mucosa-homing Treg, not resident). Treg_CCR4n_CD69p: CCR4- CD69+ (tissue-resident-like Treg without skin/mucosa bias). Treg_CCR4n_CD69n: CCR4- CD69- (resting non-homing Treg). Useful co-markers: CD103 is a widely used Trm co-marker and IS in panel — CCR4+ CD69+ CD103+ most closely matches the core skin/mucosa-homing Trm-Treg phenotype in many tissues, though CD103-negative tissue-resident populations also exist. Tissue context (mirroring Step 9): in blood samples CD69+ reads as early activation, not residency.
